_readme: Bibliographic manifest for the BS EN ISO 12215 small-craft standard series, plus the related ISO 12217-2 stability standard, as cited by src/structural/ and docs/.
This file records WHICH standard, edition and clause/table numbers a given calculation is traceable to.
It intentionally contains no normative text, formulas, or reproduced tables from the standards themselves:
ISO/BSI documents are copyrighted and this repository is public (shipshape-marine/solar-proa, published to
solarproa.org). Source PDFs are held locally by the design team and are not redistributed via this repo.
When a code module cites a clause/table number, it should also be listed under that standard's
'cited_by' entries here so this manifest stays the single source of truth for citation provenance.

standards.title: Small craft — Hull construction and scantlings — Part 3: Materials: Steel, aluminium alloys, wood, other materials
standards.role: Material requirements (steel, aluminium, wood). Used here for aluminium alloy family classification.

clauses_used.summary: General: non-heat-treatable vs heat-treatable aluminium alloy groups; both sea-water resistant; treated-alloy properties may be reduced after welding.
Non-heat-treatable alloys: major alloying element Mg (+ Mn or Si); typical use is rolled products (sheet/strip/plate) — 5000-series.

Heat-treatable alloys: major alloying element Si (+ Mg and/or Mn); typical use is extruded products (sections, bars, closed profiles) — 6000-series. This is the family the aka/mast extrusions fall under.
Al-Cu and Al-Zn alloy groups (2000/7000-series) should not be used for small-craft construction without special protection.
Documentation requirement: material data sheet must state chemical composition, grade, temper condition, minimum mechanical properties, AND minimum/expected mechanical properties after welding.

standards.title: Small craft — Hull construction and scantlings — Part 5: Design pressures for monohulls, design stresses, scantlings determination
standards.role: Design pressures and material design-stress allowables for monohull panels/stiffeners. Applied here to the vaka (main hull) as a monohull; NOT applied to global aka/crossbeam loads (see ISO 12215-7 instead).

clauses_used.summary: Design category factor k_DC (A=1.0, B=0.8, C=0.6, D=0.4).
Dynamic load factor k_DYN (planing k_DYN1/k_DYN2; displacement/sailing craft use k_DYN=3 for k_L purposes only).
Area pressure reduction factor k_AR, function of design area A_D and k_R (differs for plating vs stiffeners).

Slamming correction factor k_SLS for light and stable sailing craft. Neutral (1) in design categories C and D; in A and B it is neutral only for craft heavier than a length-based threshold, otherwise it follows from the maximum righting lever up to 60 deg heel, L_WL and m_LDC (never below 1). RP2 is under the threshold, but at Category C k_SLS = 1.
Table 13: design pressures for sailing craft bottom/deck/side (P_BS, P_DS, P_SS).
Table 17: design stresses by material/method, e.g. aluminium stiffeners sigma_d = 0.7*sigma_yw (welded), sigma_d = min(0.6 sigma_u, 0.9 sigma_y) if unwelded.

Mechanical properties and design stress of metal plating (B.1) and stiffeners (B.2) by alloy/temper, incl. EN AW-6061 closed profile T5/T6: sigma_u=245, sigma_uw=165, sigma_y=205, sigma_yw=115 N/mm2, design stress sigma_d=0.7*sigma_yw=81 N/mm2 (welded).

standards.title: Small craft — Hull construction and scantlings — Part 6: Structural arrangements and details
standards.role: Qualitative load-transfer / connection detailing good practice. NOTE: the numeric bonding-width / k_j tabbing formulas in this standard (Clause 7.2 'Bonding') are specific to FRP/composite construction and do NOT apply to the aluminium aka-to-vaka joint. For metal construction, this standard gives only qualitative good-practice principles (no closed-form joint capacity formula) — flagged explicitly as a gap in iso_joint_check.py.

clauses_used.summary: General load transfer: concentrated loads shall be transmitted via stiff supporting members/brackets, not landed on unsupported plating; avoid knife-edge load crossing (6.3.5).
Floating frame guidance (by analogy): weld or glue area at a stiffener-to-support connection should generally not be less than the stiffener web area.
Metal construction: structural continuity, no abrupt section changes, taper >=33% where section changes.
End connections: 'shall provide adequate end fixity and effective transmission of the bending moment and shear force into the supporting member' — qualitative requirement only, no formula given.
Good-practice welding (Annex C) and riveting: rivet diameter >= thickest plate thickness or 25% of total connected thickness; edge distance >=1.5x plate thickness; rivet spacing >=2.5x diameter.

Other loads to be considered with local reinforcement: docking, lifting, grounding, towing, anchoring, berthing/mooring, road transport. Not explicitly quantified by ISO 12215. Only lifting is checked in this repository (lifting_sling.py) - listed as an open item.

standards.title: Small craft — Hull construction and scantlings — Part 7: Determination of loads for multihulls and of their local scantlings using ISO 12215-5
standards.role: THE governing multihull standard — resolves the monohull-vs-proa applicability gap for global crossbeam/aka loads. Confirmed in hand (Downloads copy, first edition 2020-11) rather than assumed absent.

clauses_used.summary: Crossbeam definition for catamarans/trimarans.
Global load cases GLC1-GLC6 and the conditions under which each must be checked for a given structural arrangement.
Design stresses under global loads: aluminium alloys sigma_d = 0.7*sigma_yw, tau_d = 0.7*tau_yw (welded); non-welded properties apply if not welded.
GLC1: diagonal torsional moment in quartering sea, M_TD = 0.5*k_DC*m_LDC*9.81*k_DYNM*0.076*L_DIAG / 1000 (kNm).
GLC2 rig loads (per ISO 12215-10) combined with GLC1: 0.5*GLC1+GLC2 or GLC1+0.5*GLC2, whichever greater.
GLC5: longitudinal force on one hull/float, e.g. trimaran float F_LT = min(5*m_LDC, 5*m_FLOAT) kN, distributed to crossbeams by relative EI.
Technical background: torsional moment resisted by differential bending of crossbeams (treated as built-in at the hull, strain-energy method); worked example for a 2-beam catamaran.

standards.applicability_caveat: This standard's worked formulas and Figure 9 structural-arrangement categories assume symmetric catamarans/trimarans (two equal hulls, or one main hull + two equal floats). RP2 is a Pacific-proa layout: ONE main hull (vaka) + ONE asymmetric outrigger float (ama). Formulas keyed to 'trimaran float' (e.g. GLC5) are used here as the closest available analogue for the single ama, engineering judgement applied and flagged explicitly wherever used — this is not a literal fit and is the residual, irreducible gap even with Part 7 in hand.
standards.source_location_note: Digital copy on file is named ambiguously (iso_12215_small_craft_hull_construction_and_scantlings_7_compress.pdf); content verified page-by-page to be ISO 12215-7:2020, first edition.

standards.title: Small craft — Hull construction and scantlings — Part 10: Rig loads and rig attachment in sailing craft
standards.role: Rig/mast wind loading. Already used by src/structural/mast_analysis.py prior to this work; edition reconciled against the newer 2020 copy as part of this effort.

clauses_used.summary: Wind force on sail F = 0.72*V^2*A (case b, multihull SC1) — matches existing mast_analysis.py citation; see reconciliation note in iso_traceability.md.
Any relevant engineering method may be used to estimate stress evaluation — matches existing mast_analysis.py citation.

standards.title: Small craft — Stability and buoyancy assessment and categorization — Part 2: Sailing boats of hull length greater than or equal to 6 m
standards.role: Assigns the design category (which sets k_DC and k_SLS in ISO 12215-5/-7) and defines the safe-wind-speed / reefing information for multihulls. Design Category C is the design team's target (2026-10-15); the Clause 7 assessment itself has not been carried out yet.

clauses_used.summary: Definition of catamaran; states that proas are asymmetric catamarans, so RP2 falls under Clause 7, not the monohull Clause 6.

Minimum operating condition (light craft plus crew allowance by hull length, plus normally carried stores). The condition that Clause 7 stability requirements and Annex G use; not computed in this repository yet.
Design categories A and B require a fully enclosed boat - one reason Category B is not RP2's target.

Owner information must give the apparent wind speed at which sail should be reduced, by Annex G or sailing trials, and use the lower of the stability and rig-strength limits. Basis for treating the mast check as a strength limit alongside the reefing envelope.
Reefing safety sign at the main control position; capsize warning sign if the boat is susceptible to inversion.
Bare poles factor, and minimum maximum transverse righting lever by design category for catamarans. RP2's GZ curve does not meet the Category B value; Category C is marginal (vaka side only).

A catamaran is susceptible to inversion if its Annex G reefing wind speed falls below a category-dependent threshold; consequences in 7.12 (buoyancy when inverted) and 7.13 (escape) for habitable boats.
Meaning of design category C (Beaufort 6 or less, significant waves up to 2 m). Context for keeping the 25 kn mast design wind.

Determination of safe wind speed information: wind speed limit from the limiting righting moment and the moment of sail and windage areas about the centre of the underwater profile. The standard's counterpart to capsize_analysis.py; not yet implemented.
